payload.feature:
LANDING PR for story #744 (tui: the fleet refresh re-folds every event of every run every 2 s, so on a 745k-event journal it never stops folding and keys lag by seconds): the kept fleet, the off-loop reader, and decision 0088 (proposed).

Operator rulings and words:
- 2026-10-18, in chat, reporting #744: "with my current brokkr db, when I open the TUI and want to navigate, things are extremely slow".
- Decision 0014: readouts are read-only. Decision 0001: the journal is the hash-chained source of truth, and a readout must not show a run healthy that a whole read refuses.
- 2026-09-26, the threat model: catch realistic ACCIDENTAL misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read. A deliberate, exotic evasion is a LOW residual.
- The schema of `events` is NOT changed. The operator has a separate proposed decision (#753, decision 0089, draft PR #769) on a derived read model, in which #744's kept read becomes the fallback. Do not anticipate it here.

The branch story-744-fleet-refresh ends at 2e935439, on main 8bd34fdb (it merges clean with current main).
- 50488082 (story run implement-story-744-tui-the-flee-2046bc74): the kept fleet (fleet/kept.rs KeptFleet), the off-loop reader (tui/reader.rs, tui::behind), `brokkr runs` on the kept read, tui_views moved to src/tui_read.rs, decision 0088.
- f5a0800a answered the first review's seven findings.
- Fix rounds 744b (b5790ad6), 744c (82dca088) and 744d (15acdc32) answered three security holds on one class: a kept run carried healthy through a journal replacement that keeps its head. The final shape:
  - (device, inode) identity, and not-shorter;
  - a two-sided statement of the file, before the store opens and after the read;
  - every refresh counts each kept run's rows at or below its head over the (run_id, seq) key (Store::rows_through, a covering-index search), and reads a run whole when the count is not its head's seq. No file clock gates the count, so a row lost through the write-ahead log is seen at the next refresh.
  - 744d's review (residual LOW, no security residual) reproduced the WAL-held loss and a sqlite3 backup restore in a PTY, and saw both quarantined before any checkpoint.
- 2e935439 (controller, signed, test-only): the host exact-coverage gate on 15acdc32 counted 7949/7951 functions. The `.map_err` closures that carry KeptFleet::refresh's refusal out of tui_read::read_views and verbs::readouts::runs were reached by no test. fleet::kept_tests::unlisted (a journal with meta and no runs table) now makes both refuse "sqlite: no such table: runs", with two removal controls recorded in the commit.
- Measured (the branch's generator; 1,164 runs, 734,484 events, checkpoint bodies near 1 KiB; release build, warm): the whole read 3.48 s at 2.11 GB; the first kept read 0.48 s at 81 MB; an idle refresh 35–37 ms at 81–85 MB peak (the count 18.7–20.4 ms of it), reading 0 events.
- Host exact coverage on 2e935439 is 100% (62495/62495 lines, 8156/8156 branches, 7951/7951 functions), and host lints and ratchets hold. One host run before it failed only on the load-driven broker flake capability_broker::protocol::a_server_that_never_answers_ends_at_the_startup_deadline (protocol.rs:674), in code this story does not touch.
- Listings: quality/public-api/brokkr-store.txt gains one line, `Store::rows_through`. No file-lines, too-many-lines, suppressions or clone baseline moves.

Every review position, panel member or chief, is READ-ONLY: it changes no tracked file and makes no commit, whatever this text asks below. It reports each finding. Only the implement phase fixes a finding the review returns.

Judge, on the HEAD binary and tests (the base is the merge-base 8bd34fdb):
1. The acceptance: on a generated journal of the operator's shape, an idle console refresh reads 0 events and an append of N reads N. A key is redrawn with a read still out. Measure the idle refresh yourself.
2. Decision 0001: no path shows a run healthy that a whole read refuses, except the residual 0088 ruling 2 names. Try a replacement at the same head through a different write path from the reviews before (for example a new file renamed over the path, a truncate-and-rewrite, a WAL-held change, or a copy with the head row intact and a middle row gone), and see each quarantined with the whole read's exact text. Say whether the residual 0088 ruling 2 names is the only one left. On the 744d chief's refinement (a writer that also drops events_seq_is_a_position and replaces seq 1 by a row at seq <= 0 keeps the count and head), say whether 0088 ruling 2's words should widen to "rows at or below the head changed at the same count and head".
3. Decision 0014: every read opens the journal read-only and writes nothing (no WAL enabled, no migration, no repair), including the count.
4. Standards: CC 15 or under and 100 lines or under for every new or changed function (cargo crap); quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api (the one brokkr-store line); 744b's frame fix (terminal::held_to, terminal::unread, reader.rs Asked::frames) intact; decision 0088's every Binding: names a test that exists and asserts what it says.
5. Scope: brokkr-cli fleet/, tui/, tui_read.rs and its tests, verbs/readouts.rs, fleet.rs, brokkr-store read.rs and its tests, decision 0088, its README row and the one API line. Nothing under contracts/, fixtures/, policy/ or reference/; no engine, protocol or schema change.
6. For the PR: name every ruling needed. Expected: (a) accept decision 0088 as proposed; (b) its ruling 2 residual (a row at or below a kept head changed at the same count and head: a trigger-defeating writer or corruption SQLite reads cleanly; the whole read, a first refresh and an entered run see it); (c) its ruling 5 (checkpoint bodies still parsed and verified on the first read), which decision 0089's Asked 4 would supersede at fleet level if accepted; (d) brokkr-store's public API gains Store::rows_through. Recommend for each.

This run lands one pull request under decision 0051, so the contribution gate can vouch for it.

For the implement phase only: if a finding returns the branch, fix exactly that finding and prove it with a test bound by a compiling mutation. Then run, all clean: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test -p brokkr-store --locked; cargo test -p brokkr-view --locked; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib --locked; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it --locked (timeout 590; split by FILE:: filters if longer, and name each); typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api; `cargo crap --path <crate>/src --format json` for every function you add or change; git diff --check.

Other work runs in parallel. Decision 0065 slice two (the-forge-b9; NEVER message it, or any brokkr-wt-* seat) runs U8a2b on brokkr-runtime engine/broker* and engine.rs. #288 slice M edits brokkr-runtime agents.rs and bundle/compose.rs. #735 edits brokkr-cli recipes/agents.rs. #349 slice 8 edits brokkr-runtime dispatch sites. #753 is docs only. This landing touches none of their files.

Commit one signed-off commit ending "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>" if a fix is needed, and never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it. Run every command in the foreground: never background a command or schedule a wakeup, because a headless seat ends when it waits.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

members.adversarial:
Read-only adversarial review of HEAD 2e935439 against merge-base 8bd34fdb. No tracked files changed, no fixes or commits, no other seats contacted. No new medium/high/critical finding established.

LOW — Carry decision 0088 ruling 2's deliberate residual, with broader and more accurate wording (decision 0001; 0071 ruling 9). Sources: fleet/kept.rs:335-355 and decision 0088:76-87. Concrete input: open a healthy 105-event fixture in the HEAD console, defeat events_append_only_update and rewrite recorded_at in the envelope at seq 105, leaving indexed event_hash, row count, head, inode and file length unchanged, with the commit held in WAL. Output: the existing console remains unquarantined; whole inspect refuses and fresh runs reports exactly "chain: event 105: event_hash does not match canonical content". This is the already disclosed trigger-defeating-writer / SQLite-readable-corruption class, rated LOW by the operator's threat model, not an additional security residual. Recommend widening "a row below" to "rows at or below the head changed at the same count and head". Also do not promise recovery when the head moves: in a separate harness using unchanged production kept.rs, rewrite seq 1 beneath a healthy seq-2 fold, then append a valid EffectRequested at seq 3 through Store::append_next. Refresh reads 1 and carries healthy seq 3, while whole load still refuses "chain: event 1: event_hash does not match canonical content". Head movement alone does not reverify the prefix. Recommend explicitly accepting that lifetime as part of the same LOW residual. No additional concrete class outside that residual was established.

Independent HEAD-binary PTY probes, using imported copies of the frozen fixture, not the fixture itself: truncate the original file to zero and rewrite it from a copy missing middle event 52, preserving inode, length and head 105; next cadence quarantines with the exact whole-read text "chain: event 53: seq is not contiguous (expected 52)". Also defeat the delete and position triggers, replace seq 1 with a damaged row at seq 0, keep 105 rows and the original head; next cadence quarantines with exact whole-read text "chain: event 1: event_hash does not match canonical content". Thus the chief's seq <= 0 refinement is already caught by load_after's lowest-seq check; widening is still warranted for the head-envelope case above. Probe output and source are in .forge/review/adversarial-landing-744/probe.log and probe.py.

Acceptance: independently measured unchanged production KeptFleet, optimized standalone harness, on existing generated .forge/scratch/gen.db (1164 runs, 734484 events). First refresh read 734484 events in 851.3 ms; eight idle refreshes read 0 each and took 43.9, 40.1, 40.5, 41.1, 41.8, 42.8, 44.6 and 47.7 ms, including read-only open and row derivation. The generated 500000-event binding test passed its 500000/0/3/0 work-count assertions. The production-source selected-run idle test and gated key-redraw test passed. 744b held_to/unread/Asked::frames and their run/participant/hearth regressions remain intact.

Decision 0014: inspected every changed opening path, including whole-read worker connections and rows_through. All use Store::open_read_only / Access::Read; count is SELECT only, with no WAL enable, migration or repair. PTY probes checked unchanged main-journal bytes across inert reading. Decision 0088's Binding references resolve to existing tests whose assertions support the described work counts, replacement/WAL failures, transient retry, selection invalidation, failure bound and immediate close; the 23 focused CLI tests and 3 store read tests passed. Recorded compiling removal controls were inspected in the story commits; this read-only seat planted no mutations.

Standards/scope: fmt, workspace all-target/all-feature clippy with -D warnings, ratchet files/clones/api and diff-check passed. Fresh cargo-crap reports for CLI and store: read_views and terminal::drive CC 14, KeptFleet::refresh 6, KeptRun::carried 8, Reader::ask 10, Store::rows_through 2; no new/changed function over its allowance found. No size/suppression/clone baseline moves. Exactly one public API addition, consumed Store::rows_through. No contracts/, fixtures/, policy/, reference/, engine, protocol or events-schema changes. The key redraw with a read out is bound by tui::reader_tests::a_key_redraws_while_the_first_read_is_still_out (green) and the 744b frame fix is present: terminal::held_to (terminal.rs:194), terminal::unread (:172), reader Asked::frames (reader.rs:87, used at :132).

(2) DECISION 0001 / 0088 ruling 2: every replacement scenario I planted quarantined with the whole read's exact words - the kept row's detail words equal Store::load's error string in all of them: (A) a row deleted while held in a write-ahead log with no checkpoint - caught by the count (6 != 7) with the journal file byte-identical, i.e. no file clock gates the count; (B) a damaged file renamed over the path (new inode, head kept); (C) the original truncated to zero and rewritten in place from a copy missing a middle row - same inode, same length; (D) the chief's refinement - seq 1 replaced by a damaged row at seq 0 with both the delete and the events_seq_is_a_position guards dropped, so 7 rows at or below a head of 7 - is caught: the carry refuses (load_after's RowBeforeChain on MIN(seq)=0) and the run is read whole, quarantined 'chain: event 1: event_hash does not match canonical content' exactly as the whole read says. No widening of the count is needed for it. (H) The head row's indexed event_hash column tampered: the carry refuses and the run is read whole (7 events), and the whole read itself loads clean - the two reads agree, no stale row. The RESIDUAL, reproduced by me: the head envelope itself (E) or a row below the head (F1) rewritten in place, at the same row count and the same head, in a file that keeps its inode and length, is carried - the fleet shows the run folded and healthy (words None, state seq 7, 0 events read) while the whole read refuses 'chain: event N: event_hash does not match canonical content'; and (F2) after the head moves by one valid append through the store's own path, the fleet still carries (1 event read) and shows the run folded - the changed rows are never re-verified. So the head row is inside the class too, and the class outlives head movement: ruling 2's words should widen from 'a row below a kept head' to 'rows at or below the head changed in place at the same row count and the same head'. The widening changes only words, not code - the count already covers the whole prefix, and the head is confirmed by its indexed event_hash column, which an envelope rewrite leaves alone. That widened content class is the only residual my probes found: row presence (lost or added below the head, including at seq 0), file identity (device+inode), length, the head hash column, and head movement are all caught. One observation, not a residual: recount covers only folded runs, so a run kept REFUSED at an unmoved head is re-shown as it was while its rows change beneath it - already ruling 2's refusal sentence (a refusal of the journal's own bytes is kept at its head), the row shows a refusal, not a fold, and any head movement re-reads it whole.
